replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: I rarely get anxious about math itself, but I do feel stressed when it’s tied to deadlines or complex problems in work. My neuroticism score is moderate, so I manage stress through hobbies like photography and baking, which help me stay calm.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: I used AI tools like Wolfram Alpha for quick calculations and explanations last year. It helped me understand basic concepts faster but wasn’t great for advanced topics. I prefer hands-on practice over automated solutions.
replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, write the equation in standard form ax² + bx + c = 0. Then calculate the discriminant b² - 4ac. If it’s positive, two real solutions; if zero, one real solution; if negative, complex solutions. Finally, plug into the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(b²-4ac)] / (2a).

To find stationary points, take the derivative f'(x), set it equal to zero, and solve for x. Plug each x back into f(x) to get the y-values. These points are where the function might have maxima or minima. Always check the second derivative to confirm if it’s a peak or valley.
